we have designed a protein that forms a two-dimensional lattice with a negative Poisson’s ratio (auxeticity) that undergoes a fully reversible change in lattice parameters.

the design, synthesis and characterization of a new class of coherently dynamic, 2D crystallites with auxetic properties, which are of interest for the development of new functional materials.
the design of dynamic, coherently moving 2D protein crystals, and the demonstration of auxeticity in 2D materials.
the design of self-assembled 2D crystallites with precise spatial arrangements.

the C98RhuAs are the first example of a 2D protein lattice with the capacity to undergo large-scale motions while retaining crystallinity.
this work demonstrates a design strategy for the self-assembly and dynamic reconfiguration of unsupported two-dimensional crystalline lattices.
the self-assembly and dynamic behaviour of C98RhuAs 2D latices is unprecedented.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have designed and assembled coherently dynamic, auxetic, 2D crystallites from a single protein.
we have developed a simple and general strategy for the design of dynamic two-dimensional protein lattices, and demonstrated their unique properties and potential applications.
we have designed a 2D protein lattice that can be coherently deformed by 30 per cent without losing crystallinity.

it is possible to design protein lattices that are both dynamic and coherently crystalline.
